Page 1 intro: A poem/song (366) for every day of the year by Tom Jensen... INDEX - There is a helpful index located on page 376 that includes the title of the poem or song, what page it is on and also what subject category it is listed under. I am really good at three things in this world. One of them is writing lyrics for songs with the occasional poem tossed in every so often for style points. There's five spoofs at the end, too! About This: I've been writing poems and song lyrics for over twenty years. In 2007 I put a bunch of my poems onto YouTube videos and asked musicians to turn them into songs. Many of them did. Fast forward 13 years and I have collected up all the best things I've written and arranged them in order from MY BEST ones to ones that aren't quite as good. I ranked all my babies so you can just start reading the best stuff right away. Stop reading them anymore, no problem... See how far ya get! I'm opening ALL my lyrics up to musicians again. Time to spread our wings... readtom.com is my website. cards.item_type: NO HOME IN THE TREE YET · BOSTON GLOBE EDITOR LETTER
cards.summary: Typed letter on Boston Globe letterhead to Tom Jensen, signed by John Yemma, Deputy Managing Editor, Sunday.
cards.typed_words:
The Boston Globe
Dec. 12, 2002

Dear Mr. Jensen:

Thank you sending your articles on Manny Ramirez and on Common Sense. I'm afraid I can't see them working in the Globe news pages, which is my area of concentration. In news articles -- even feature articles -- we take more of a dispassionate, third-person approach than you have taken in the pieces you shared with me. I'm not sure what would be your most appropriate forum for these articles -- perhaps an opinion magazine.

This is not to say that you shouldn't try to sell future articles to different departments of the Globe. If you decide to do so, I would recommend that you study the articles in a particular section, come up with an interesting idea involving unique reporting that seems in sync with articles that already appear in that section. Then I'd suggest that before writing the piece you pitch the idea to the editor of that section (you can find the names of the editors on our Web site, "www.boston.com/globe" or in Editor & Publisher). Free-lance writers that I have worked with have succeeded by filling a need an editor might have and then establishing a working relationship with him or her. That is the best way to break into the business. Rarely are over-the-transom articles published.

Best of luck to you in your writing career.

Sincerely,
John Yemma
Deputy Managing Editor, Sunday
